newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Soft commodities out of favour.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Soft commodities out of favour.

text.p: Soft commodities continued to lose their attraction for investors and prices for both cocoa and coffee fell quite sharply.
In other commodites, rainfall caused prices to fall in Chicago grain pits, recently voaltile metal markets stabilised although gold continued to recover from recent lows.
On the London International Financial Futures Exchange (LIFFE) cocoa prices suffered a 3.7 percent loss on the day as speculators unloaded their holdings.

Reduced concern over supplies seemed to have changed market sentiment from that which took the September futures price up to 1,170 sterling a tonne at the start of the month. It finished Monday at 985 sterling.
Analysts reckoned the new season's crop at the world's leading p roducer, Ivory Coast, was developing strongly with large harvests possible if favourable weather continued into August.

Also, there was a growing feeling that the affect of the El Nino weather phenomenon, where a warming of the Pacific Ocean off South America affects tropical weather patterns, may come too late to influence upcoming cocoa crops.
LIFFE coffee prices extended their protracted fall, dropping more than $50 a tonne as speculators glumly noted the passing of the peak Brazilian frost danger season.

U.S. independent weather forecaster Weather Services Corp said no damaging cold was in sight for the next five days in Brazil's coffee growing regions. By late July the danger of a frost usually recedes sharply.
In the U.S., week-end rainfall in Illinois, a key growing area for corn and soyabeans, saw prices for these drop sharply at the opening of Chicago grain markets on Monday.

A recent dry spell in the Midwest had threatened potential yields of these crops and boosted prices but today soyabeans dropped over 20 cents a bushel and corn over 10 cents before the markets stabilised.

The gold price moved above $328.00 an ounce at one stage on Monday as investor shortcovering continued to rally the price from its 12 year low around $314.00 set two week's ago after Australia's central bank sold 167 tonnes of the yellow metal.
